title: IMESD's Mulvihill receives lifetime achievement award
text:
IMESD’s Mulvihill receives lifetime achievement award
Published 5:00 pm Wednesday, June 17, 2026
SALEM — InterMountain Education Service District Superintendent Mark Mulvihill has received the 2026 Jerry Colonna Lifetime Achievement Award, one of the highest honors recognizing a career of service and leadership in Oregon education.
The Coalition of Oregon School Administrators gave the award to Mulvihill, according to an announcement from the IMESD.
Throughout his 38-year career, Mulvihill has served Oregon students and educators as a teacher, coach, principal, assistant superintendent and superintendent. His leadership has influenced education policy, strengthened regional and statewide partnerships, expanded opportunities for students and helped develop generations of educational leaders, according to an announcement.
Since becoming superintendent of IMESD in 2008, Mulvihill has led initiatives that have expanded educational opportunities across Eastern Oregon and beyond. Under his leadership, IMESD advanced innovative programs including the Virtual Learning Academy, the Blue Mountain Early Learning Hub, student wellness initiatives and comprehensive school safety and security efforts.
Mulvihill also has served on the Oregon Quality Education Commission, the Oregon Education Investment Board and the COSA Governor’s Advisory Committee and was president of the Oregon Association of Education Service Districts.
Regional superintendents nominated Mulvihill
Seventeen superintendents from throughout the IMESD region signed the nomination letter. The education leaders described Mulvihill as a “trusted mentor, advocate and leader” who defined a career with service, innovation and an unwavering commitment to public education.
The letter also states Mulvihill has “consistently ensured that small, rural and urban school districts alike have a strong and equitable voice in statewide conversations” and credits him with helping shape funding models, advance equity-focused policies and support system-wide improvements that continue to benefit Oregon students and educators today.
Beyond his formal leadership roles, Mulvihill has been committed to developing future educational leaders. Through his work as a Regional Administrative Licensure Program coordinator, adjunct faculty member, mentor and community leader, he has supported aspiring administrators and educators across the state.
“His transformative leadership, steadfast advocacy, and deep commitment to public education have shaped programs, influenced policy, and inspired generations of students, educators, and leaders across Oregon,” the IMESD superintendents wrote in their nomination letter. “His legacy is defined by service, innovation, and excellence, and his impact will continue to be felt for years to come.”
COSA formally recognized Mulvihill on June 17 at its annual conference in Seaside.
